questions.q: Why can too much funding hurt a young startup?
a: It breeds complacency instead of focus
It forces the team to hire too slowly
It attracts competitors to the same idea
It makes customers distrust the product
questions.why: Lesson 1 says excess money can breed complacency, while leaner startups know what is necessary and get it done.

questions.q: What happened to Duke Nukem 3D's sequel?
a: It stayed in development for 12 years and never shipped
It shipped early and sold poorly
It was cancelled before the first game launched
It was sold to another studio and became a hit
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the sequel, stuck in development for 12 years after the first game's success, as a cautionary tale.

questions.q: What mistake did Webvan make, according to the summary?
a: It overestimated demand and lost a billion dollars
It underestimated costs and ran out of drivers
It ignored competitors and cut its prices
It expanded too slowly and lost customers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Webvan's weak market research led it to overestimate purchases by 60 percent before filing for bankruptcy.

questions.q: What does the summary say about a startup's plan in its early days?
a: It will change often, and that is normal
It must be fixed before the first sale
It should stay hidden from customers
It matters less than the founder's passion
questions.why: Lesson 2 notes that an early plan will go through many changes, which is normal, before settling into a solid model.

questions.q: How did Craigslist handle its growth?
a: The founder promoted an employee to run management
The founder sold the site to a larger rival
The founder hired a team of outside consultants
The founder kept control of every decision
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes Craig Newmark promoting Jim Buckmaster to take over management as the site grew.
